resources.string: Android\'s global proxy (%1$s) is off while zaptun is connected, so every app goes through zaptun. It comes back when you disconnect.

Android\'s global proxy is set to %1$s, so apps that use it bypass zaptun. To let zaptun switch it off, run: adb shell pm grant dev.davidjosearaujo.zaptun android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, then reconnect.
%1$s is a system CA, so every app trusts ZAP.
%1$s is only a user CA: Chrome and debuggable apps trust it, most apps don\'t. Click Intercept in ZAP to install it as a system CA (needs root).
ZAP\'s CA isn\'t installed, so HTTPS won\'t decrypt. Click Intercept in ZAP\'s Android Devices dialog to install it (needs root).
Tap a port to remove it. Connections to other ports go straight to their destination.
No ports: nothing goes to ZAP.
Also find HTTP on every other port

Other ports are looked at for half a second: plain HTTP, and TLS that offers HTTP (ALPN), go to ZAP. Anything else still goes straight to its destination, a little later if the server speaks first (SSH, SMTP). Add a port above to send any TLS on it to ZAP.
Every app is intercepted except the ones switched off (%1$d).
Only the apps switched on are intercepted (%1$d).
Enter a host and a port between 1 and 65535
No connections yet. Anything an app opens through zaptun shows up here, intercepted or not.
UDP passed straight through (ZAP can\'t proxy it): %1$s
UDP refused, so clients fall back to TCP: %1$s
DNS queries: %1$d, without an answer: %2$d, retried over TCP: %3$d
This resets the ZAP address (%1$s:%2$d), the intercepted ports and the app selection (all apps). If zaptun is connected, it reconnects.
